# Rocket.Chat Adapter

Development preview of a text-only bridge between direct WhatsApp conversations and Rocket.Chat Omnichannel.

## Features

- Direct WhatsApp text → a Rocket.Chat visitor and Omnichannel room.
- Agent plain-text replies → the mapped WhatsApp conversation.
- Session, department and origin isolated visitor credentials and room mappings.
- Bounded persistent inbound retry queue, deterministic Rocket.Chat message IDs and reply deduplication.
- Host-verified webhook secret; visitor echoes, transcripts, internal notes and attachment messages are ignored.

## Setup

1. Have OpenWA **≥ 0.30.0** and Rocket.Chat Omnichannel enabled, with an available agent and any required department configured.
2. Link a WhatsApp test session. Copy its OpenWA session UUID.
3. Install this plugin, then set `baseUrl`, `sessionId` and optionally `department` in its configuration. Enable it only for that WhatsApp session.
4. Mint a **session-bound** ingress instance. Choose a random secret locally, then configure the **same** secret in Rocket.Chat:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://your-openwa-host/api/integration/plugins/rocketchat-adapter/instances' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"instanceId":"support","sessionScope":"<SESSION_UUID>","secret":"<RANDOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET>","config":{"baseUrl":"https://rocket.example.com","sessionId":"<SESSION_UUID>"}}'
```

If you use `department`, set the same value on the plugin configuration and on the instance. The instance and hook must resolve to the same origin, department and session, or their mappings are deliberately isolated. Use one instance per session/destination.

5. In Rocket.Chat **Omnichannel → Webhooks**, set the URL to `https://your-openwa-host/api/ingress/rocketchat-adapter/support/omnichannel`, paste the secret as **Secret Token**, and subscribe to **Agent Messages**. OpenWA checks `X-RocketChat-Livechat-Token` before dispatching to the worker and acknowledges accepted deliveries with HTTP 200.
6. Send text from a consenting test number to the linked WhatsApp session. Accept the room in Rocket.Chat and reply with plain text.

No Rocket.Chat administrator API token is required by the plugin: it uses the visitor REST API with a random per-chat visitor token. An administrator is still needed to configure Omnichannel, agents and the webhook.

## Install

```bash
npm ci
node package.mjs rocketchat-adapter
```

Upload `rocketchat-adapter.zip` in OpenWA → Plugins → Install. It installs disabled. Configure it before enabling. This preview has not been published as a GitHub Release.

## Configuration

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | yes | Rocket.Chat HTTPS origin only, without paths, credentials, queries or fragments. |
| `sessionId` | yes | Exact OpenWA session UUID; must also match the ingress instance's session scope. |
| `department` | no | Department name or ID supplied to visitor registration. Changing it starts a separate mapping namespace. |
| `deadLetterAction` | no | `none` (default), `replay` or `clear`. |
| `deadLetterActionId` | for replay/clear | Fresh operation ID: 1–100 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores. |

### Configure and activate

From the OpenWA Plugins page, open the adapter's configuration and save:

```json
{
  "baseUrl": "https://rocket.example.com",
  "sessionId": "<SESSION_UUID>",
  "department": "Support"
}
```

`sessionId` is the OpenWA session UUID, not its display name or phone number. Omit `department` if you do not use departments. In the plugin's session selection, choose only that session, then enable the plugin. For an additional session, use a matching per-session override and its own session-bound ingress instance.

The equivalent REST commands are:

```bash
curl -X PUT 'https://your-openwa-host/api/plugins/rocketchat-adapter/config' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"config":{"baseUrl":"https://rocket.example.com","sessionId":"<SESSION_UUID>"}}'

curl -X PUT 'https://your-openwa-host/api/plugins/rocketchat-adapter/sessions' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"sessions":["<SESSION_UUID>"]}'

curl -X POST 'https://your-openwa-host/api/plugins/rocketchat-adapter/enable' \
  -H 'X-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>'
```

Use an unscoped ADMIN key for these management routes. The webhook secret is separate from the OpenWA API key. Generate it with `openssl rand -hex 32`, keep it private, and use exactly the same value in the ingress instance and Rocket.Chat. Secret values must be 16–512 characters.

### Docker laboratory

Use the [official Docker deployment guide](https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/deploy-with-docker-docker-compose). Keep published ports on localhost and put the services on a shared private network.

The distributed plugin accepts **HTTPS only**, including in a lab. Put a TLS reverse proxy in front of Rocket.Chat, use its HTTPS origin in both configs, and install the lab CA into OpenWA's Node trust store using `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. For an internal hostname, add only that hostname to the host's `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. Do not disable TLS verification or SSRF protection globally. No lab hostname is shipped in the manifest.

Rocket.Chat may call OpenWA's internal ingress URL `http://openwa:2785/api/ingress/rocketchat-adapter/support/omnichannel` inside an isolated Docker lab. Public ingress must use HTTPS.

### Dead-letter maintenance

The plugin settings expose `deadLetterAction` (`none`, `replay`, `clear`) and `deadLetterActionId`. After resolving an outage, select `replay` and provide a fresh ID, for example `retry-2026-11-11`. Save the config for the affected origin/department/session. The action also runs when that resolved per-session config next dispatches an event. Base-config maintenance runs on save/enable without network calls.

- `replay` resets retained failures into the pending queue up to its available capacity. Ambiguous deliveries retain their original room and visitor token. Entries conflicting with a newer visitor/room mapping stay retained; they are not silently redirected.
- `clear` discards retained failed messages only. It does not delete visitor mappings or active pending work.
- A repeated action ID is a no-op across saves/restarts (last 100 IDs retained). Use a new ID for another attempt; the fields may remain saved unchanged. Health reports pending/dead counts for active destinations. Inspect the maintenance count log to see how many were replayed, cleared or retained.
- Retention is at most 100 dead letters for seven days, independent of the 100 live pending slots. Expired/oldest records are removed on the next state mutation, with a count-only warning. Clear/export failures before that deadline if needed.

## Compatibility

Targets OpenWA **≥ 0.30.0**. The plugin is marked **development**, not stable. Unit/contract tests and local verification are summarized below; `testedOpenWAVersion` is a host verification baseline, not a live WhatsApp guarantee.

Rocket.Chat reference environment: 8.0.1 with Omnichannel visitor, room, message and message-history REST endpoints. A workspace without available agents may refuse room creation; the plugin retains the message for retry rather than claiming delivery. Confirm your edition's Omnichannel availability before deployment.

### Per-session config

Supported by re-reading `ctx.config` for each hook/webhook. This first version explicitly binds a config to `sessionId`: other sessions are ignored. Each session needs a matching bound ingress instance. Origin, department or session changes fence pending operations and select a separate durable namespace; they do not migrate existing visitors, rooms or pending work. Old queues remain stored and require an operator decision before reuse.

### Limits and delivery semantics

- One-to-one `text` messages only, at most 4096 characters. No media, captions, groups, calls, contacts, polls, edits, deletions, quoted replies, own-phone message mirroring or automated handover. Unsupported inputs are ignored.
- Disable overlapping bot responders for the test session. This plugin is an observer at priority 20; it does not silence bots when an agent takes a room.
- At most 500 active/recent chat mappings per destination/session. Least recently used mappings without pending/in-flight work are evicted when a new contact arrives; this is not a lifetime contact ceiling. Old room replies after eviction are ignored. Dead letters keep a token snapshot for replay. If every mapping is pinned, enqueue fails explicitly until work completes. Live pending capacity is 100, separate from dead-letter retention. A rejected enqueue/storage failure is not guaranteed recoverable.
- Inbound work runs off the hook path; a crash before durable enqueue can lose that event. Four workers drain up to 100 due items per pump, preserving FIFO within each chat. A retrying chat does not block other customers. Provider I/O runs outside the short storage lock, so slow Rocket.Chat calls do not hold up agent replies. Five attempts use increasing delays before dead-letter retention.
- Pending queues survive restarts, but draining resumes only after that resolved destination/session dispatches a hook or webhook. In-memory destination caches are cleared on disable or config changes.
- An ambiguous Rocket.Chat send is reconciled against the last 100 messages in its pinned room using the deterministic message ID. It is never automatically moved to a new room. A closed/unreadable room or an old message outside that window can leave work dead-lettered for manual resolution.
- Outbound delivery is **at least once**. Successful sends are marked afterward: a crash, storage failure or ambiguous WhatsApp timeout can produce a duplicate on retry. At most 500 recent reply IDs and 500 successful inbound IDs are remembered per namespace. Host ingress also deduplicates byte-identical webhook bodies.
- Relay exceptions deliberately omit provider response bodies, URLs containing visitor tokens, message text and contact identities. Health retains a failure indication until re-enable or a valid config/maintenance save; inspect and resolve retained work first. “Healthy” means no failures observed since enable, not verified provider connectivity.

## Verification and troubleshooting

1. Confirm the configured WhatsApp session is connected in OpenWA.
2. In Rocket.Chat, add the operator as an Omnichannel agent and set the agent to **Available**. Confirm membership/availability in the configured department, if any.
3. Send a new plain-text message from another consenting WhatsApp number. Confirm one Omnichannel room/message appears, then reply from the agent UI and confirm one reply arrives on WhatsApp.
4. Repeat after restarting OpenWA and with another contact to check persistence and recipient isolation. Enable/disable decisions persist across restarts; disable the plugin when finished testing.

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| OpenWA login says Invalid API key | Use the key for the running OpenWA installation. A separate Docker data volume has a different bootstrap key from a previous npm installation. |
| Webhook returns 401 | The Rocket.Chat Secret Token must match the ingress instance secret; do not use the OpenWA admin key here. |
| Authenticated webhook returns 503 | The bound WhatsApp session must be connected and the plugin restored/enabled; the route has a session-alive preflight. |
| No Omnichannel room appears | Check the origin, exact session UUID, plugin activation, agent availability and department. A provider/room failure is retained for retry. |
| Network request refused | For public deployments use a reachable HTTPS origin. For a Docker lab check the HTTPS proxy, CA trust and exact internal-host SSRF exception. |
| Agent reply is not delivered | Match plugin and instance origin/department/session settings, select Agent Messages, confirm plain text and inspect plugin health/host logs. Unknown rooms or mismatched visitor tokens are acknowledged and ignored, without sending to WhatsApp or degrading health. |
| Health remains degraded after recovery | Inspect retained pending/dead-letter work and fix the cause before re-enabling. Do not delete plugin state to clear the warning: it contains visitor credentials, room mappings and dedup markers. |

Initial verification used OpenWA 0.27.1 and Rocket.Chat 8.0.1. The revised adapter requires and was installed in OpenWA 0.30.0; a real inbound LID message updated an existing Rocket.Chat visitor with the resolved telephone number, verified in Contact → Details after refreshing the page. Automated tests cover protocol filtering, retries, persistence, destination/session isolation and lifecycle behavior; real visitor/room/message/history APIs were exercised in Docker. The tester also reported successful bidirectional WhatsApp messaging, a restart, a second contact and no duplicate messages in those checks. This is limited manual evidence, not a guarantee for every deployment or exactly-once delivery.

The adapter sends a phone number when the chat JID is a real telephone identity (`@c.us` or `@s.whatsapp.net`, device suffix stripped). For privacy IDs (`@lid`), the `engine:read` capability first checks the host canonical mapping, then the contact's authoritative phone JID. The lookup is limited to 1.5 seconds and is retried on subsequent messages, including for existing visitors. If WhatsApp cannot resolve the phone, delivery continues without it. Privacy IDs and unverified `Contact.number` values are never presented as telephone numbers.

## Development

```bash
npm run typecheck
node --import tsx --test rocketchat-adapter/*.test.ts
npm test
node package.mjs rocketchat-adapter
node scripts/loader-check.mjs rocketchat-adapter
npm run catalog
npm run catalog:check
```

Keep the copied `chat-lock.ts` identical to the other plugins listed in `scripts/shared-copies.test.mjs`. Manifest metadata and the dated changelog drive generated catalog/Details blocks; do not hand-edit them.

## Security

Only a verified, session-bound webhook can send. Recipients come exclusively from persisted room **and visitor-token** mappings, never a phone number supplied by the webhook. Visitor tokens, inbound text and queued messages are sensitive plugin state; protect the OpenWA data volume and backups. No real credentials belong in commits or fixtures.

Report vulnerabilities privately using the [OpenWA security policy](https://github.com/rmyndharis/OpenWA/security), never a public issue. Plugins execute trusted host code; the worker is not a boundary against a malicious plugin.
